qified_examples.question: What do official returns and recorded campaign spending establish about the race, equally for both candidates?
known: A Nov 11 secondary snapshot reports 36,624 for Aaron Gutierrez and 30,759 for Dana Charles; 5,865 spread and 8.704 percentage points of candidate votes; unofficial, not certified.
Colorado Files displays candidate committee raised/spent $149,182/$111,989 for Gutierrez and $132,973/$100,378 for Charles; different reporting cycles and update times must not be silently mixed.

Colorado Files defines independent expenditure totals in four for/against cells, adding to $2,331,240 under its allocation method. These are not candidate committee receipts or causal effectiveness measures.
County Nov 5 notice estimates 1,036 countywide outstanding ballots; not SD3-specific.
positions: Candidates and committees: what official filings say
Independent groups: spending for and against both candidates
Community: historical outcomes and transparent reporting, no individual targeting
unknowns: certified SD3 vote total
each candidate/committee's post-election corrections, transfers, debts, and filing IDs
whether Atlas author's stated security features can be independently inspected
any causal impact of Atlas, advertising or fieldwork on the vote
qified_examples.next: Obtain official certified district vote report and individual TRACER amended committee and IE notices. Normalize period and de-duplicate according to record IDs. Publish precinct results only where appropriate and aggregate.

qified_examples.scope: Pueblo County FY2026 adopted vs FY2027 proposed
qified_examples.question: Is the County 2027 budget adopted and what is the reconciled recurring financial position?
known: County's official 2027 budget page links preliminary proposed budget, calendar and presentations; its adopted section was empty at the November 12 check.
County management's priorities page describes a 15% of eligible General Fund personnel budgets targeting $9.81 million and work on monthly reporting and controls policies.
These management statements are not proof that proposed changes were enacted, recurring savings realized, or all interfund positions reconciled.
positions: County: public proposed budget and finance reform narrative
Independent review: ask for verified recurring bridge, fund restrictions and monthly actuals
Service users: evaluate practical service and equity impact separately
unknowns: adopted 2027 ordinance or resolution
verified operating cash and fund restrictions by period
implementation and service-level impacts
qified_examples.next: Track adoption, verify line-item bridge and fund restrictions, reconcile transfers and performance by department.

qified_examples.scope: Project Falcon; Lime Road; St Charles industrial area
qified_examples.question: Which public commitments and road obligations exist, and how much has actually been paid?
known: Open Publica's Oct 26 Council meeting summary reports a 7-0 vote approving an option-to-purchase ordinance for Project Falcon.
An option to purchase is not itself a demonstrated completed land sale, construction milestone, realized job count or cash disbursement.
The circulating $65 million combined public-investment claim remains un-reconciled across components in this master packet.
positions: City and economic-development advocates: intended jobs and investment
Infrastructure and taxpayer critics: cost, road ownership, timing and transparency
Affected industrial employers and workers: road usability and service reliability
unknowns: final executed instrument, parcel IDs and valuation
Lime Road documented ownership and maintenance responsibility
commitment-by-fund, payment-by-entity, obligations and clawbacks
contractor and employer compliance data
qified_examples.next: Read primary ordinance and executed option, historical roads records, grants, title, audited payments and independent engineering condition records; construct no-double-count ledger.

qified_examples.scope: Pueblo Heritage Center former railway freight station
qified_examples.question: What legal and financial consequences would any disposition produce, and what alternatives exist?
known: Colorado Public Radio reported Nov 11 the city has listed a city-owned former railroad freight station housing Pueblo Heritage Center for sale.
CPR attributes an appraisal exceeding $1.9m and a $300,000 nonprofit offer to statements made by Mayor Graham; these are not independently audited valuations in this packet.
CPR also reports museum-group concerns and council members seeking reconsideration; listing is not evidence of a completed sale.
positions: Administration: property consolidation, appraisal and fiscal stewardship
Historical Society/heritage advocates: institutional history, grant-funded rehabilitation and cultural continuity
Council and public: evaluate alternatives, process, stewardship conditions, and nearby rail-planning context
unknowns: deed, appraisal document and scope
grant restrictions and preservation covenants
lease and occupancy agreements
executive-session/legal authority and executed disposition status
qified_examples.next: Read title/appraisal/council authorizations and grant restrictions; compare retain, lease, public sale, nonprofit sale and conservation arrangements using validated costs and rights.

qified_examples.scope: Pueblo camera enforcement and related privacy controls
qified_examples.question: What was authorized, how are data, fines, procurement and outcomes governed?
known: Oct 26 independent Council summaries report 5-2 approval of an Automated Enforcement Coordinator position.
The staffing vote alone does not prove cameras are deployed, revenue offsets realized, safety outcomes delivered, or privacy practices effective.
positions: Public safety rationale: road safety and enforcement consistency
Privacy and civil liberties: retention, access, discriminatory effects and mass-surveillance questions
Financial review: vendor payments, revenue assumptions, legal challenges and independent outcomes
unknowns: signed vendor agreement and all ordinance IDs
citation amounts, appeals, cost and net revenue by period
data retention, sharing, access, audits and deletion rules
measured crash/speed changes with comparable baseline
qified_examples.next: Retrieve signed agreements, council record, police policy, annual finances, complaint/appeals totals and road safety indicators; separate predictions from observed outcomes.

qified_examples.scope: PACOG metropolitan transport and infrastructure crosswalk
qified_examples.question: Which routes and projects are planned, financed, obligated, built and operating?
known: PACOG's published program page links 2025–2028 TIP, a TIP tracker, FY2025 obligated projects and its 2050 LRTP, adopted in April 2026.
A programmed improvement is not necessarily fully funded, let, completed or operating; route and parcel data have independent time versions.
positions: Regional planners: forecast mobility and long-range needs
Local residents/business: current conditions, costs, access and construction impacts
Funding partners: federal/state/local eligibility and obligated deliverables
unknowns: latest executed project agreements and payment data
GIS layers and vintage/license compatibility
baseline transport performance and impacts by community
qified_examples.next: Normalize TIP/LRTP IDs to CDOT grants, contracts, completion, jurisdictional road status and spatial geometry. Report 2020/2030/2040/2050 models as scenarios, not observations.
